records.region: Southern Peru, eastern Huarpo–Santiago upper corridor through the Ica and Ocucaje valleys to the Pacific near Monte Grande.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Three acquired original MTC maps support the complete selected headward, junction, valley and coastal corridor as part of the Río Ica system. The upper selected route occupies the Huarpo–Santiago corridor rather than the northern Olaya or Tambo headwaters. The observed reach-name changes prevent a whole-feature scalar naming claim but do not leave a material geographic gap.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative downstream river-system identity, not a uniform hydronym for every selected reach
records.completion_scope: The three independently issued, successfully acquired MTC originals resolve every material selected corridor and junction through the actual coastal outlet. Río Ica is supported as the representative downstream system identity. The explicit upstream Huarpo/Santiago distinction limits name scope without creating a material source gap. Optional source failures do not add a second pending classification.

component_scope_limits: Río Ica is the representative downstream identity. It is not assigned to all upstream tributary reaches.

The district sheet labels the eastern upper corridor Río Huarpo and the continuation past Santiago de Chocorvos Río Santiago. The precise naming extent of the first short selected headward segment is not established and remains null.

The northward Olaya and Tambo branches are material junction context, not additional selected mainstems. The department and district maps are generalized cartography and do not establish a formal naming-register record.
No exact channel-bank, vertex, present-day perennial-flow or terminal-point naming claim is made.

records.supported_name_scope: Owens River is a bounded middle/lower channel identity. Other locally observed creek, lake and canal names remain component/context identities only; no representative whole-system name is supported.
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: The full selected geography is covered, including the Adobe closed-basin lake/wetland chain, intervening Black Lake–Benton terrain, episodic Tri-Valley wash/canal transition, named Owens River, reservoir passage and dry-lake terminal extension. These are an observed composite, not one supported whole-route hydronym. The mapped divide and non-channel lake-bed extension are scope limitations rather than missing-source gaps.

naming_scope_details.not_selected_alternative_upstream_corrid: Natural upper Owens River–Lake Crowley–Owens Gorge route lies separately to the southwest.
scope_limits: No continuous named river is assigned across the Adobe Valley closed-basin terrain or the Black Lake–Benton divide.
No perennial link or groundwater-to-surface identity is inferred for the Tri-Valley transition.
Fish Slough, Hutchinson Creek, tributaries, canals and lake interiors retain distinct feature scopes.
The final selected lake-bed extension is not the mapped Owens River channel.
No exact source, legal naming boundary, exhaustive tributary inventory, current flow state or cause of model/map disagreement is established.

records.region: Eastern California, North Canyon/Adobe Valley, Benton/Hammil/Chalfant country and the Owens Valley to the Owens Lake dry bed.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected FID starts in the North Canyon/Adobe Creek setting, traverses Adobe Valley’s lake and wetland complex, crosses intervening terrain toward Benton and follows Spring Canyon Creek and the Chalfant wash/canal country into the Owens River. It then follows the Owens corridor through Tinemaha Reservoir and the lower valley before extending across the Owens Lake dry bed. Complete original cartographic coverage supports a name-scope hold, with no whole-object candidate.
records.completion_scope: Complete original geographic review at ordinary component/corridor scale. The full selected geography is covered, including the Adobe closed-basin lake/wetland chain, intervening Black Lake–Benton terrain, episodic Tri-Valley wash/canal transition, named Owens River, reservoir passage and dry-lake terminal extension. These are an observed composite, not one supported whole-route hydronym. The mapped divide and non-channel lake-bed extension are scope limitations rather than missing-source gaps.

records.region: Northeastern Venezuela, Turimiquire–El Guamo headward setting, middle Guarapiche and lower tidal wetlands toward Río San Juan.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Río Guarapiche is supported in the selected middle corridor, with broad upstream El Guamo and downstream San Juan context. The acquired cartography does not resolve the selected lower wetland passage among Caño Francés, Dos Aguas and other branches through to its actual terminal. This is a genuine material-coverage gap, not a completed naming-scope hold.
records.supported_name_scope: Partially supported river-corridor candidate; full selected representative-system correspondence remains pending.
records.material_pending_reason: Upper selected drainage and its complete passage into and out of El Guamo are not resolved by detailed original cartography. Material lower Guarapiche–Caño Francés/Dos Aguas wetland branching and the selected continuation to Río San Juan remain unresolved. The actual selected terminus within the San Juan tidal system has not been established independently of model sea metadata.
records.completion_scope: The single selected FID was considered throughout, but only its middle corridor has sufficient original cartographic correspondence. Upper El Guamo passage, lower wetland branches and the actual selected terminal remain unresolved.

component_scope_limits: Río Guarapiche identifies a supported middle river corridor. It is not assigned to every selected headwater, reservoir passage or tidal channel.
Caño Francés, Caño Dos Aguas, Caño Toro and Río San Juan retain separate identities. Their regional association cannot determine which named lower branches the selected line follows.
El Guamo remains a separate reservoir name. The broad map is insufficient to establish the complete selected headward-to-reservoir passage.
The selected downstream end is in the San Juan tidal-river/wetland setting at generalized regional scale; a direct Gulf of Paria outlet is not established for this selected feature.

records.supported_name_scope: Epenche, El Veladero, La Minera, Agua Zarca, Tejocote, Tamazula, Tuxpan, Naranjo and Coahuayana remain bounded component or adjacent-channel identities. Coahuayana is not promoted to a representative name for the entire selected composite.
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: Original cartography covers the complete selected geography, including the Mesa de Mota interfluve between the northern El Veladero/La Minera drainage and the Agua Zarca–Tejocote return, and the actual Boca de Apiza terminal. The selected object is a mapped composite of local channels, intervening non-channel terrain and the downstream Tamazula–Tuxpan–Naranjo–Coahuayana corridor. No whole-object hydronym or continuous surface flow across the interfluve is supported. This is a completed name-scope hold, not a missing-source or undecidable-connector gap.

scope_limits: No name or perennial/continuous surface flow is assigned across Mesa de Mota.
Names of source-study regional stems are not automatically applied to the selected Epenche head.
Trojes storage, Amela lagoon, canals and lateral feeders remain distinct.
El Tejolote on the municipal map and El Tejocote on the finer cartography are reported as source-specific labels, not verified official aliases.
Primary hydrographic prose is not a formal-name registry verification.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
